sources.entry: MonitorControl - Control external display brightness and volume directly. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/MonitorControl/MonitorControl/) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]
MonitorControl - Control your external monitor brightness, contrast or volume directly from a menulet or with keyboard native keys.

summary.one_liner: MonitorControl is a free macOS menu bar app that controls external display brightness, contrast and volume (and native Apple brightness/media keys) and shows the native macOS on-screen display.
summary.what_it_does: The app adds menu bar sliders for each connected display and lets you adjust brightness, volume and contrast, including through the keyboard's native brightness and media keys or custom shortcuts. It uses several protocols: DDC/CI for most external monitors (hardware brightness, contrast, volume), Apple's native protocol for Apple and built-in displays, gamma table control for software dimming, and shade (overlay) control for AirPlay, Sidecar, DisplayLink and other virtual screens. It can sync multiple displays to a single slider, smooth brightness transitions, and dim to full black. Many advanced options are available under "Show advanced settings" in Settings. The README notes it is installable via Homebrew and built from source with Xcode.
use_cases: control external monitor brightness from the Mac menu bar
adjust external display volume or contrast
use Mac keyboard brightness keys on an external monitor
dim multiple displays together with one slider
software dimming for TVs and virtual screens
how_to_run: Download the latest .dmg from the Releases page and copy MonitorControl to Applications
Grant Accessibility permission in System Settings if you want native brightness and media keys
notable: Combines DDC hardware dimming with software dimming to go below the monitor's minimum brightness
Supports DDC, native Apple protocol, gamma tables and shade overlays across display types
Shows native macOS OSD for brightness and volume
Syncs built-in/Apple display brightness changes to external monitors
caveats: No DDC control over the built-in HDMI port on some Intel and M1/M2 Macs; use USB-C or software dimming instead
DisplayLink docks and EIZO-type displays get software dimming only
Limited native OSD percentage display on macOS Tahoe; macOS 27 needs v4.4.0 or newer; older macOS versions have limitations
